Messages.Author: legb...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
i've just been reading the Revealing cards thread. Thought-provoking
stuff and some of the language indicates that the Fire hasn't gone out of
our collective belly since the 7/7, erm, debate. i want to make a comment
and ask a question.

COMMENT: While i personally don't have a strong view on the PRINCIPLE of
the new rules [no notes, no sneak peeks] i do worry about the
practicality of enforcing them - "what you cannot enforce, do not
command" as Noal's sig file puts it. i'm fairly sure that John
"Dreadjudge" Eagles will share my worries - John? Are you listening? And
in Jyhad on-line e-gossiping behind other players' backs is a large part
of the game and doesn't detract from the conspiratorial aspects at all,
quite the contrary.

QUESTION: How does the new rule affect the Succubus club? "OK, it's my
untap. During it [dear predator] i will swap you this card in my hand for
Gitane's Inverary castle. It's an AI, i promise, and your only chance of
staving off the malky sneak-bleeders for which your deck is so PITIFULLY
unprepared. No, you can't look at it before we clinch the deal - VEKN
rules forbid that. You will just have to take my word for it." Somehow
that doesn't seem right to me.

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

I'd like to comment on the way of enforcing that "rule". How do you
prevent a player from revealing a threatening card like a Bum's Rush or
other nasties? Imho it is impossible. If i really want to show the card
under the new rules, i can just drop it on the table, either by
"clumsiness" or apologizing and saying that i played the wrong card ("i
bleed with GtU! _shows Bum's Rush....oops!)
Apart from having a judge behind each player pondering if the "reveal
card" action was intentional or not, i guess there is no way to enforce
that rule. Besides over here, the tournaments are much closer to social
events than ultra-competitive environments ala Magic. In my (old?) days
i used to play magic, and got really tired of the tournament attitude,
the "don't do this, don't do that! or be disqualified" thing.
I do understand that one of the arguments put forward in favor of the
rule are that flashing a card to an opponent to scare him or her, or it,
is "bad" because you should just have to use poker-like techniques to
persuade yr prey that you have the said card. ok some people like to
play that way and bluff is always good :)
However many others play differently and the ability to show cards can
play a great part in their strategy i.e. combat decks: if you bleed/vote
against/do any nasty thing to me i will crush you! hey look i do have
the means of enforcing what i said. I do think this is the only way to
calm down a dedicated sneak-bleed...and it saves time, showing the card
instead of spending half an hour trying to convince a thick-headed not
to bleed just to hear yr predator says: "bleed with GtU...and
conditioning"...sigh....
My point is, again to quote Noal's sig file, "what you cannot enforce,
do not command", trying to enforce the rule will only lead to situations
like this: "judge, he showed a card! No i didn't, it fell! no you showed
it on purpose....etc ad nauseum....followed by kindergarden
whining....did not, did to, did not....
Oh well, I never have to show any card when i have Beast on the
table...maybe an IG?
Regards, P.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Ah. Saying "I'll trade you this card, whatever it is" is different than saying
"I'll trade you an AI". If you don't agree to trade an AI, then of course, you
don't have to trade an AI.

However, your phrasing - "I'll trade you this card - it's an AI" would be
suspect, and could easily get you in trouble with the judge. I'd be clear
about the terms of the trade ("this card") and what it was I was just talking
about ("It's an AI, I promise").

> The way you are ruling this at
> the moment, it seems to me you would have to warn me for unsportsmanlike
> conduct if i lied about the pre-terms of a KRC in order to prevent
> someone from blocking.

The nature of the card being traded is not a "pre-term" of the trade - it is
a term of the trade. If you wish to make it a pre-term, you should be clear -
that the term is just "this card" and, as an additional note, but not a term
of the trade, it may be (and you assert that it is) an AI.

Likewise you cannot "lie" about the terms of the KRC when you announce
them (after having not been blocked) - you can't "lie" and say "I'll get 3 and
my prey gets 1" and then, after the votes are in, say "Oh, that wasn't quite
true, the actual terms were that my prey gets 3 and my grand-prey gets
1".


